title: Service Reliability Integrator Initiative Charter
content:
Purpose and elevator pitch:
This brief defines a 12-week experiment to establish a ‘Service Reliability Integrator’ (SRI) role and lightweight runway to accelerate SLO adoption across feature teams. The SRI is a rotating cross-functional liaison embedded with product teams for short sprints to translate SLOs into actionable implementation and operational handoffs.

Why now:
- SLO adoption velocity is uneven: some product squads ship without SLO translation or measurable alerts.
- We need a repeatable, low-friction pattern to operationalize SLOs for model-serving features (routing, caching, kv-cache warmup).
- The goal is pragmatic: surface measurable improvements in error budgets, alert fatigue, and oncall readiness without adding heavy governance.

Success criteria (12 weeks):
- 6 product services have an SLO translated into clear alerting + a readiness checklist onboarded to the SRE-runbook.
- Median time-to-resolution on model-serving latency regressions drops by 18% for participating services.
- Feature teams report the SRI process reduced ambiguity in deployment runbooks (survey target >= 80% positive).

Scope (what we will and will not do):
- In scope: SLO definition translation, alert tuning, runbook authoring, playbook handoffs, one canary rollout plan per service, and a lightweight measurement dashboard template.
- Out of scope: Full platform instrumentation rewrites, heavy refactors, contractual SLA negotiations with customers.

Roles and staffing model:
- Service Reliability Integrator (SRI, 0.5 FTE per cycle): rotates every 6 weeks; primary responsibilities: pair with product engineers, draft SLO interpretation, create alert runbooks, and validate canary rollout steps.
- SRE Sponsor (0.1 FTE): approves SLO targets and escalation ladder; triages conflicts.
- Product Partner (0.2 FTE): team-designated engineer and PM who own execution within the product team.
- Observability SME (ad-hoc): assists with dashboards and metric instrumentation.
- Program Lead (Marcus Liu): runs the experiment cadence, recruitment, and retrospective.

Cadence and timeline (high level):
- Week 0: Launch and shortlist candidate services; orientation deck and 1-hour kick-off.
- Weeks 1–2: Discovery + baseline telemetry (latency/error budget, call graphs, traffic patterns).
- Weeks 3–4: Draft SLO interpretation (golden signals, service-level indicators), initial alert set, and canary plan.
- Weeks 5–6: Implement alerts & runbook; first SRI rotation handoff; baseline endline capture.
- Weeks 7–10: Iterate based on first cycle feedback; refine templates and checklist.
- Weeks 11–12: Consolidate artifacts, playbook publication, and retrospective.

Deliverables (per service):
- SLO interpretation doc: plain-language description, SLI queries, threshold rationale.
- Alert matrix: which alerts fire to whom, expected noise-level, and escalation path.
- Oncall runbook snippet: triage steps, quick mitigations, rollback signal, and runbook links.
- Canary rollout checklist: traffic split plan, safety gate metrics, rollback criteria.
- Measurement snapshot: baseline metrics and end-of-cycle metrics.

Templates and tooling we will provide:
- A canonical SLI query template (Prometheus/Datadog compatible) with examples for model-serving (inference duration P50/P95, kv-cache hit rate, token throughput).
- Runbook snippet template with triage flow, contact matrix, and suggested mitigation steps: scale-up, model-fallback, ky-memory clear, routing failover.
- Lightweight dashboard template with P50/P95 latency, request error rate, evicted-kv-keys, and capacity headroom.

Onboarding checklist for product teams (quick):
- Confirm service owner and PM.
- Provide traffic profile, recent deploy cadence, and incident postmortems (last 6 months).
- Grant read access to telemetry and alerting tools.
- Accept the canary experiment constraints and fallback policy.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: SRI becomes a bottleneck if too many services are queued. Mitigation: cap to 2 concurrent SRIs and maintain prioritized backlog.
- Risk: Feature teams ignore recommended alerts because they feel noisy. Mitigation: require a 2-week measurement window to show alert noise delta before sign-off.
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps delay progress. Mitigation: Observability SME triage and a short-term shim approach (synthetic probes).

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-minute sync with product partners and SRE sponsor.
- Slack channel #sri-program for async questions and quick decisions.
- Bi-weekly show-and-tell for leadership (10–15m): measured wins and blockers.

Measurement approach and example metrics:
- Primary signals: SLI correctness (does query match intent), SLO burn rate, incident lead time, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to repair (MTTR), and paging volume per 1k deploys.
- Example SLOs to test translation patterns:
  - Inference latency SLO (per-region): 99% of requests under 400ms for production-small-seq model variant.
  - Availability SLO: 99.9% successful responses (non-500) measured daily excluding planned maintenance windows.
  - Correctness proxy SLO: model feature-dependent metric (rerank hit rate > X) — used only for business teams.

Open questions (to resolve in Week 0–1):
- Should we mandate a minimum telemetry retention window for services to be eligible? (proposal: 30d)
- How much authority does SRI have to flip alerts to production or require a rollback?
- Can SRIs make small instrumentation changes (adding tags to spans) or do they need an RFC per change?

Next actions (short to-do):
- Identify 8 candidate services and prioritize top 6 (Marcus, by 2025-03-21).
- Recruit first SRI rotation volunteer and confirm schedule (Aisha).
- Build SLI template and one example for serving-runtime (Observability SME).
- Create Slack channel and schedule Week 0 kick-off (Priya).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Keep playbook minimal — teams prefer concrete triage script > long governance docs.
- Document real examples: capture one incident where caching avoided a full model fallback — that narrative sells the practice.
- Consider a small incentive: SLO-badging for teams that complete runbook onboarding (sticker / listing in team directory).

Appendix: Quick SLO translation checklist (one-liner):
1) Who is the customer of this SLO? (internal infra / external)
2) Which RPCs/paths are in scope?
3) What is the error budget window? (30d / 7d)
4) Which SLI query maps to the above?
5) Where should alerts land and what is the escalation?
6) Canary safety gates and rollback triggers

End of doc.
